evidence.summary: Header comment: 'Readr: reading lists and 1-5 star ratings' (consistent with the code).
SQLite via sqlite3, hard-coded file readr.db, one module-level connection; no commit anywhere.
books table: id integer primary key, title text not null (no author).
lists table: id integer primary key, name text not null.
list_books join table: list_id references lists(id), book_id references books(id); no primary key or uniqueness, so the same book can be added to a list twice.
ratings table: book_id references books(id), stars integer, with no CHECK constraint.
rate(book_id, stars) raises ValueError('1 to 5 stars') unless stars is one of 1..5, then inserts a new ratings row (appends).
add_to_list(list_id, book_id) inserts a list_books row with no validation of either id.
The whole app is two library functions: no HTTP server, CLI or UI; no function creates, renames, lists or deletes lists or books, or removes a book from a list.

architecture.backend: a Python module exposing rate() and add_to_list() over one SQLite connection; no entry point

features.name: Rate a book (1-5 stars)
features.description: Give a book a whole-number rating from 1 to 5 stars.
features.observed_behaviour: rate(book_id, stars) rejects anything but 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 with ValueError, otherwise inserts a ratings row. Rating again appends another row.
features.business_logic: stars in {1..5}, checked in code only (no database CHECK). No user on a rating; appended, never updated.
features.integration: Same scale and same append behaviour as Shelfie's rating; needs the unified Book.

features.name: Reading lists
features.description: Put books on named reading lists.
features.observed_behaviour: add_to_list(list_id, book_id) inserts a list_books row. Lists have a required name. Nothing in the code creates, renames, shows or deletes a list, or removes a book from one.
features.business_logic: list name required; a list holds many books and a book can be on many lists (many-to-many); duplicates are not prevented; ids are not validated.
features.integration: Needs the unified Book, list create/view/remove operations (absent in Readr) and per-user ownership.
subfeatures: add a book to a list (observed)
create / view / rename / delete a list (schema only, no code)

entities.name: Book
entities.description: A book that can be rated or listed (title only).

entities.name: ListBook
entities.description: A book on a list (table 'list_books'); duplicates possible.

entities.name: Rating
entities.description: One star rating given to a book; appended.

auth.model: none: a local library with no users

error_handling.behaviour: ValueError('1 to 5 stars') raised to the caller

error_handling.case: unknown list or book id in add_to_list
error_handling.behaviour: accepted silently (no validation; SQLite foreign keys off by default; inferred)

unknowns: How lists and books are created, viewed or deleted: the tables exist but no code does it (the user would know whether another front end existed).
Whether writes persist: no commit is ever called (inferred from sqlite3 defaults; code not run, running source code not approved).
Whether duplicate list entries and multiple ratings per book are intended.
How Readr is meant to be used (no entry point: imported by something not in the folder?).
